title: DetailView's own record header repeats the title/action width arbitration hazard fixed in page:header
body:
Split out of #7244 (renderer-side fix landed on `page:header`). Not measured in a browser — identified statically while fixing the sibling header, and filed rather than fixed to keep that PR to one verified change.

## What #7244 fixed

`packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx` laid the record header out as a `flex-nowrap` row: a `shrink-0` action tail plus a `flex-1 min-w-0` title column. The title column, being the only flexible item, absorbed the whole width deficit — measured at a 799px viewport, header 687px, tail 641.5px, leaving the h1 **29.5px**. Fixed with an `sm:min-w-48` floor on the title column plus `sm:flex-wrap` on the header.

## The same shape elsewhere

**1. `packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx:919` — same shape, no protection.**

```
div.flex.flex-col.sm:flex-row.items-start.justify-between.gap-3.sm:gap-4.pb-4.border-b
  div.flex.items-start.gap-2.sm:gap-3.flex-1.min-w-0     <- title column, no floor
    div.flex-1.min-w-0
      h1.text-xl.sm:text-2xl.font-bold.truncate
```

No `flex-wrap` on the row and no width floor on the title column — the two things whose absence produced the reported bug. This header is the one that renders when the host does NOT supply a `page:header` (the file's own comment: suppressed when the host page renders its own `page:header`), so it is a live path, not dead code.

**2. `packages/layout/src/PageHeader.tsx:236` — partially protected.**

Its outer row is already `flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-4 gap-y-2`, so the deficit has somewhere to go. But the title column is still `flex flex-col min-w-0 flex-1` with no floor, and `flex-1` means a flex-basis of 0 — so the column never contributes width that would force a wrap, and a wide `slot` sitting on the same line still takes the remainder. Milder, same root.

## Why this is worth its own card

The fix for each is a judgment about that layout (is a floor right, what value, should the row wrap), and each lives in a different package with its own build and test surface — so verifying them properly means a browser repro per header, which #7244's PR deliberately did not take on.

## Suggested check

Drive a record whose header carries three or more labelled actions at a viewport around 800px through each path, and read `h1.getBoundingClientRect().width` against `h1.scrollWidth`, the way #7244 was measured.
